stem: Candle P is 30 centimeters tall and burns down at a constant rate of 2 centimeters per hour. Candle Q is 20 centimeters tall and burns down at a constant rate of 0.75 centimeter per hour. The two candles are lit at the same time. After how many hours will the two candles have the same height?
solution: After \(t\) hours, candle P is \(30 - 2t\) centimeters tall and candle Q is \(20 - 0.75t\) centimeters tall.
So \(t = 8\). (Both candles are then 14 centimeters tall.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. 14 centimeters is the common height of the candles, not the number of hours.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This finds when candle P loses the 10-centimeter difference (\(10 \div 2\)) but ignores that candle Q is also burning down.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses \(20 + 0.75t\) for candle Q, a sign error that makes it grow instead of burn down.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'B': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'B'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
t = symbols('t')
sol = solve(Eq(30 - 2*t, 20 - Rational('0.75')*t), t)
assert sol == [8] and 30 - 2*8 == 14
assert value(choices[answer]) == sol[0]
assert all(value(choices[k]) != sol[0] for k in choices if k != answer)
